We had a shared modal component, but to fit his own page, he just copied it and made some custom changes.
It saved time at first, but create the duplicated code.

Then I suggested a solution.
I said, let's make the modal configuration driven.
We can use props to control the content, actions, and buttons.
That way, no need to copy the whole component again.
He liked the idea and we refactored it together.

Five.
That conflict with my teammate made me realize we needed unit tests to avoid bugs when updating it later.
So I add the full test coverage.
Now, whenever we change the modal, we just run the test to make sure everything still works.
It helps prevent regressions.
Looking back, I think the conflict wasn't a bad thing.
It pushed us to do better.
